> I'm unsure how to create an MRP of this issue. Can anyone advise on that ?

Create new project, try follow your own "steps to reproduce". Before `5. Click the **Bucket Fill** tool icon.` be sure to save your project. If clicking the bucket tool results in freeze, you can upload such saved project as the MRP.
If you can't reproduce this way then the steps to reproduce are not sufficient / need to be more detailed.

^^^ This happens after Godot 4.6 crashes on my PC due to the issue. So I'm gonna try restarting my PC and reloading a new project. 

Update: I was able to create an MRP in a new project. 

[terrain_MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25318798/terrain_MRP.zip)

I've added an MRP with my files, and created a short video showing exact error: www.youtube.com/watch?v=ApuFMxeVTJk&feature=youtu.be

After some research, it appears that this could be user error or me misunderstanding how terrains work, but in general, **here's how to trigger the bug:** 

1. Create Project
2. Create Node 2d
3. Create tile map layer and save it
4. Add an atlas
5. Map out Grass and Dirt terrain
6. Fill in the map layer with base grass, just empty grass square
7. Add the grass variants (i.e. flowers, grass types) with scattering randomly across the map layer to get different grass types
8. Select terrain type i.e. grass, dirt terrain, and then select Bucket fill
9. Error triggers repeatedly: ERROR: Condition "p_terrain_set < 0" is true.
   at: TerrainsPattern (scene/resources/2d/tile_set.cpp:322)


It seems like it's trying to reference a terrain set that is set to -1. But I'm not sure why it's trying to do this even in a fresh project.

I was able to reproduce the issue in 4.6 and previous versions with simpler steps: 1. Create the `TileMapLayer` node 2. Add a `TileSet` resource 3. Go to the `TileMap` tab, select the `Terrain` tab and the `Bucket Fill` mode 4. Move the mouse in the scene https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/770e7a9b-d773-450b-9954-38e89906d6a2

In the MRP the error stops if the `Terrain` property is setted on the `TileSet` https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ee5c213-8505-448d-82f8-b21170025bb0

Probably this is not a bug but just the editor complaining about the missing config, but the way that happens is too chaotic as can freeze the editor because the error spam. Maybe change the way as this error is shown for the user for something like the script editor do or as a node warning.

Note that this kind of backtrace it pretty much useless (besides kinda confirming it indeed crashed for you). You'd need to run a build with [debugging symbols](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/engine_details/development/compiling/introduction_to_the_buildsystem.html#debugging-symbols) to get relevant stack trace (but doing so is not required as long as others can reproduce the issue).

@JRDK92 Also note I've fixed [your YouTube link](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/116267#issuecomment-3902687563), and previously `rsubtil` fixed formatting etc. in [the issue description](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/116267#issue-3940022641) (you can check edit history). > (...)

This results in the same error spammed indeed, but apparently that's a different case than the one originally reported here: in one you have a valid terrain selected when trying to bucket fill, in the other you don't.

> Probably this is not a bug but just the editor complaining about the missing config, but the way that happens is too chaotic as can freeze the editor because the error spam. Maybe change the way as this error is shown for the user for something like the script editor do or as a node warning.

I'd say that's definitely a bug. There's no reason why it should show internal errors to the user. For the no valid terrain selected case you've shown maybe it would make sense to show some kind of info/warning within the TileMap dock itself, but it should still not result in internal errors.
